subject: Political Science
central_question: Which principles and institutions can distribute rights, rewards, resources and opportunities fairly while protecting the dignity and prospects of the least advantaged?
in_scope_units: What is Justice: traditions, Socrates, well-being, giving each person their due and human dignity.
Equal Treatment for Equals, Proportionate Justice and Recognition of Special Needs.
Just Distribution, redistribution and equal life conditions.
John Rawls’ Theory of Justice and the veil of ignorance.
Pursuing Social Justice through a basic minimum and the debate between free markets and state intervention.
banned_topics: Detailed affirmative action and competing ideologies of equality, which belong to Equality.
Detailed categories of political, economic and cultural rights, which belong to Rights.
Detailed economic policy instruments and development planning, which belong to Economics.

known_pitfalls.claim: Justice means helping friends and harming enemies.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter rejects this narrow idea and connects justice with the well-being and due of all people.

known_pitfalls.claim: Equal treatment always requires equal rewards regardless of effort or skill.
known_pitfalls.correction: Proportionate justice allows relevant differences in reward while maintaining equal basic rights.
It may extend equality when a relevant disadvantage blocks equal participation or opportunity.
The veil of ignorance is designed to make fair rules follow from ordinary rational self-interest.

known_pitfalls.claim: Social justice requires absolute equality of lifestyle.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter seeks basic conditions, fair opportunity and reduction of deep deprivation rather than complete sameness.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Exercise Q1 on giving each person their due.
Use NCERT Exercise Q2 to compare the three principles of justice.
Use NCERT Exercise Q3 to test special needs against equal treatment.
Use NCERT Exercise Q4 to explain Rawls’ veil of ignorance.
Conclude with NCERT Exercise Q5 on the basic minimum and government responsibility.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises contain Questions 1–6 on due, principles of justice, special needs, Rawls, basic minimum conditions and state action.
